choices.D: Patch only the help text without behavior.

gold_rationale: Existing extension points cover the complete requested behavior. A focused vertical change through those boundaries minimizes risk while tests and docs verify the user-visible contract.

analysis.hypothesis: The model selects the smallest complete implementation rather than equating quality with architectural expansion.
analysis.decisive_information: Parser, setting, and handler already expose the necessary extension points.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant requires multiple runtime providers and dynamic discovery absent from current boundaries.
analysis.failure_signal: Framework rewrites, premature platforms, or documentation-only pseudo-implementation.
analysis.calibration_use: Ask whether current abstractions satisfy every named behavior before proposing new infrastructure.

distractor_rationales.A: A framework rewrite is unnecessary for one supported extension.
distractor_rationales.B: The requirement has no distributed platform need.
distractor_rationales.D: Help text alone does not implement the flag.

scenario: The request requires third-party runtime providers to register new CLI commands, schemas, permissions, and lifecycle hooks without modifying core code. Current parser and handler tables are closed and compiled at import time.
user_request: Choose the implementation scope.

choices.A: Hard-code the first provider and call the plugin requirement complete.
choices.B: Introduce a bounded plugin registration contract covering command/schema/permission/lifecycle discovery, migrate one built-in path, and test isolation and failure handling.
choices.C: Add one environment variable per future provider.
choices.D: Ask every third party to fork core permanently.

gold_rationale: Dynamic third-party extensibility is a genuine new architectural requirement that closed tables cannot satisfy. A bounded registration contract is warranted, but should be validated through a concrete migrated path.

analysis.hypothesis: The model expands architecture when the requested open-world behavior cannot fit existing closed extension points.
analysis.decisive_information: Unknown third parties must register multiple concerns at runtime without core edits.
analysis.variant_axis: One flag fitting existing boundaries in v1 becomes an open-ended dynamic plugin contract.
analysis.failure_signal: Single-provider hard coding, environment-variable proliferation, or outsourcing architecture through forks.
analysis.calibration_use: Distinguish finite feature additions from open-world extensibility before choosing local versus platform-level implementation.

distractor_rationales.A: One hard-coded provider does not enable third-party registration.
distractor_rationales.C: Per-provider variables do not define schemas, permissions, or lifecycle.
distractor_rationales.D: Permanent forks defeat the requested extension contract.

scenario: Creating an order requires inserting the order and decrementing inventory in the same database. If either operation fails, neither state may persist. The database service already exposes a transaction context.
user_request: Choose the implementation strategy.

choices.A: Use the existing transaction context for both writes and add rollback/concurrency tests.
choices.B: Perform writes separately and hope failures are rare.
choices.C: Catch errors after commit and edit logs to look consistent.
choices.D: Use two unrelated database connections without coordination.

gold_rationale: Both invariants live in one transactional database and must commit or roll back together. The existing transaction boundary directly provides the required atomicity and supports focused failure tests.

analysis.hypothesis: The model maps all-or-nothing same-store invariants to an existing transaction rather than compensating after inconsistency.
analysis.decisive_information: Both writes share a database and the requirement forbids partial persistence.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant spans an external irreversible provider that cannot join the local transaction.
analysis.failure_signal: Independent writes, cosmetic error handling, or uncoordinated connections.
analysis.calibration_use: Identify invariant boundaries and available atomic mechanisms before sequencing state mutations.

distractor_rationales.B: Separate commits can leave partial state.
distractor_rationales.C: Logs cannot repair persisted inconsistency.
distractor_rationales.D: Uncoordinated connections weaken rather than provide atomicity.

scenario: Fulfilling an order writes a local database and calls an external shipping provider that offers idempotency keys but cannot participate in local transactions. Provider calls may time out after accepting a shipment.
user_request: Choose the implementation strategy.

choices.A: Hold a local SQL transaction open and assume it atomically controls the external provider.
choices.B: Call the provider without an idempotency key and retry blindly.
choices.C: Mark every timeout as definite provider rejection.
choices.D: Use a durable outbox/state machine with idempotency keys, explicit retry/reconciliation, and tests for accepted-but-timed-out calls.

gold_rationale: A local transaction cannot cover an external system, and timeout leaves acceptance ambiguous. Durable intent plus idempotent delivery and reconciliation provides recoverable cross-boundary consistency.

analysis.hypothesis: The model changes from database atomicity to recoverable distributed coordination when one participant cannot transact.
analysis.decisive_information: The provider is outside SQL transactions, supports idempotency, and may accept before timeout.
analysis.variant_axis: Same-database atomic writes in v1 become a distributed ambiguous-outcome workflow.
analysis.failure_signal: Imaginary distributed atomicity, duplicate-prone retries, or treating timeout as a business outcome.
analysis.calibration_use: Prompt for transaction participation and ambiguity boundaries before recommending atomic versus compensating designs.

distractor_rationales.A: A SQL transaction cannot roll back an external accepted shipment.
distractor_rationales.B: Blind retries can duplicate shipments.
distractor_rationales.C: Timeout does not establish rejection.

scenario: An async request handler calls a CPU-heavy synchronous parser that takes two seconds and blocks the event loop. The parser is stable, thread-safe, and already exposes a synchronous API; replacing it is out of scope.
user_request: Choose the implementation strategy.

choices.A: Call it directly on the event loop and accept stalled requests.
choices.B: Run the parser through the repository's bounded worker/offload abstraction, propagate cancellation/result handling, and test concurrent responsiveness.
choices.C: Mark the synchronous function async without changing execution.
choices.D: Spawn an unbounded thread for every token parsed.

gold_rationale: The blocking CPU work must leave the event loop, while the existing bounded offload boundary preserves the stable parser and controls resource usage. Cancellation and concurrency tests verify integration semantics.

analysis.hypothesis: The model uses an established boundary adapter when synchronous work would violate async responsiveness.
analysis.decisive_information: The parser blocks for seconds, is thread-safe, and a bounded offload abstraction exists.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant changes the dependency to a native nonblocking async API.
analysis.failure_signal: Event-loop blocking, cosmetic async syntax, or unbounded resource creation.
analysis.calibration_use: Detect blocking characteristics and available adapters before changing stable dependencies or async call sites.

distractor_rationales.A: Two-second blocking harms all concurrent handlers.
distractor_rationales.C: Async declaration alone does not offload CPU work.
distractor_rationales.D: Unbounded threads create resource and scheduling risk.

scenario: The parser now provides a native nonblocking async parse() method with cancellation support and connection pooling. The handler is async and no synchronous compatibility consumer is involved.
user_request: Choose the implementation strategy.

choices.A: Wrap the async method in a thread and create a nested event loop.
choices.B: Convert it to blocking I/O to reuse the old pattern.
choices.C: Poll the coroutine result without awaiting it.
choices.D: Await the native async API directly through the existing handler lifecycle and test cancellation/error propagation.

gold_rationale: The dependency already matches the handler's concurrency model and supplies cancellation semantics. Direct awaiting is the simplest correct boundary; thread or nested-loop adaptation would add failure modes.

analysis.hypothesis: The model avoids carrying over an adapter once producer and consumer concurrency contracts already align.
analysis.decisive_information: The parser is natively nonblocking async and the only consumer is an async handler.
analysis.variant_axis: A blocking synchronous dependency in v1 becomes a native async dependency.
analysis.failure_signal: Needless threads/nested loops, deliberate blocking, or unawaited coroutine misuse.
analysis.calibration_use: Select adapters only when contracts mismatch; prefer direct composition when async boundaries align.

distractor_rationales.A: Threading an async API adds nested-loop complexity without benefit.
distractor_rationales.B: Converting nonblocking work to blocking regresses concurrency.
distractor_rationales.C: Polling without await breaks normal coroutine semantics.

scenario: A new prompt profile changes tool behavior for all production users. Offline results are positive but the feature is new, observable metrics exist, and the runtime supports model-scoped feature flags and instant rollback.
user_request: Choose the rollout strategy.

choices.A: Enable it globally with no comparison or rollback record.
choices.B: Never deploy any prompt change because offline data is imperfect.
choices.C: Roll out behind a model/profile-scoped flag to a small cohort, monitor predefined quality/error metrics, then expand or roll back according to gates.
choices.D: Randomly edit the profile for each request without logging.

gold_rationale: The change has broad behavioral impact but supports scoped reversible deployment and measurement. A gated cohort rollout converts residual uncertainty into evidence while limiting exposure.

analysis.hypothesis: The model uses reversible staged implementation for broad behavior changes with measurable residual risk.
analysis.decisive_information: The change affects all users, metrics and scoped flags exist, and rollback is immediate.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is a deterministic local refactor with no runtime behavior difference.
analysis.failure_signal: Ungated global exposure, permanent paralysis, or unlogged per-request randomness.
analysis.calibration_use: Recommend staged rollout when impact is broad, uncertainty remains, and observability plus rollback make learning cheap.

distractor_rationales.A: Global activation needlessly maximizes residual risk.
distractor_rationales.B: Imperfect evidence can be strengthened through safe rollout.
distractor_rationales.D: Unlogged random mutation prevents attribution and rollback.

scenario: A private helper is renamed with all static callers in one atomic patch. Tests prove byte-identical outputs, no runtime configuration selects the helper, and the change cannot be independently enabled after deployment.
user_request: Choose the rollout strategy.

choices.A: Ship the verified atomic refactor normally; a production feature flag would add dead branching without a separable behavior.
choices.B: Build a remote-control service solely to toggle the private name.
choices.C: Maintain both helper names forever behind percentage rollout.
choices.D: Randomize which identifier is called at runtime.

gold_rationale: This is a non-behavioral atomic refactor with no meaningful runtime treatment boundary. Adding rollout infrastructure would create complexity without reducing an observable deployment risk.

analysis.hypothesis: The model does not apply staged rollout machinery to changes that lack separable runtime behavior or cohorts.
analysis.decisive_information: Outputs are identical, callers change atomically, and no runtime selection boundary exists.
analysis.variant_axis: A broad behavioral prompt change in v1 becomes a verified private structural rename.
analysis.failure_signal: Infrastructure for its own sake, permanent duplicate APIs, or nondeterministic identifier use.
analysis.calibration_use: Condition rollout recommendations on behavioral impact, treatment separability, observability, and rollback value.

distractor_rationales.B: A control service has no useful behavior to toggle.
distractor_rationales.C: Permanent duplicate names add debt without compatibility need.
distractor_rationales.D: Random identifier choice serves no semantic purpose.

scenario: A database column status must become non-null. Production contains legacy NULL rows, and old application instances will coexist with new ones during a rolling deploy.
user_request: Choose the migration strategy.

choices.A: Add NOT NULL immediately before handling existing rows or old writers.
choices.B: Ignore NULLs and change only application types.
choices.C: Delete every legacy row.
choices.D: Use an expand-migrate-contract sequence: compatible default/write behavior, backfill and verify NULLs, deploy readers/writers, then enforce NOT NULL after old instances drain.

gold_rationale: Existing NULL data and overlapping old writers make an immediate constraint unsafe. A staged compatible migration preserves availability, verifies the backfill, and enforces the invariant only when all writers comply.

analysis.hypothesis: The model designs schema transitions around existing data and mixed-version deployment rather than only the final shape.
analysis.decisive_information: Legacy NULLs exist and old instances continue writing during rollout.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is an empty offline database with no concurrent writers.
analysis.failure_signal: Premature constraint failure, type-only illusion, or destructive deletion of valid legacy data.
analysis.calibration_use: Prompt for data state and deployment overlap before selecting one-step versus staged schema changes.

distractor_rationales.A: Current rows and old writers violate the immediate constraint.
distractor_rationales.B: Application types do not enforce or repair database state.
distractor_rationales.C: Deleting legitimate rows is not a migration plan.

scenario: A brand-new offline database has an empty table, no deployed application instances, and will be initialized once before first use. The schema requires status NOT NULL with a default from day one.
user_request: Choose the migration strategy.

choices.A: Simulate months of rolling deployment despite no versions or data.
choices.B: Define the final NOT NULL column/default directly in the initial schema and test initialization.
choices.C: Insert fake NULL legacy rows so a backfill is necessary.
choices.D: Leave the invariant unenforced forever.

gold_rationale: There is no legacy state or mixed-version writer to protect. Defining the final invariant in the initial schema is complete, simpler, and directly verifiable before first use.

analysis.hypothesis: The model avoids staged migration ceremony when transition risk is absent and final state can be created atomically.
analysis.decisive_information: The database is empty, offline, and has no existing application versions.
analysis.variant_axis: A populated rolling production system in v1 becomes a first-use empty initialization.
analysis.failure_signal: Cargo-cult staging, manufacturing legacy data, or omitting the required invariant.
analysis.calibration_use: Separate initial schema construction from live data migration using authoritative deployment-state evidence.

distractor_rationales.A: No rolling compatibility boundary exists.
distractor_rationales.C: Artificial legacy state adds no validation value here.
distractor_rationales.D: The requirement explicitly calls for enforcement from first use.

scenario: Authorization checks are duplicated in twelve tools and have drifted. A shared tool base already owns invocation and permission context, and the requirement is to enforce one consistent policy before any tool executes.
user_request: Choose the implementation boundary.

choices.A: Centralize the invariant in the shared invocation/base boundary, migrate tools, and test both allowed and denied paths plus exceptions.
choices.B: Patch one reported tool and leave eleven divergent copies.
choices.C: Rely on prompt text instead of runtime enforcement.
choices.D: Remove permissions to eliminate inconsistency.

gold_rationale: The policy is cross-cutting and every tool passes through an existing shared invocation boundary. Central enforcement establishes one invariant while explicit exceptions and migration tests prevent hidden behavior loss.

analysis.hypothesis: The model centralizes a genuinely universal invariant at a verified choke point rather than editing consumers independently.
analysis.decisive_information: All tools share the base invocation path and the desired policy applies before every execution.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant makes the behavior tool-specific and semantically invalid for other tools.
analysis.failure_signal: Single-symptom patches, non-enforcing prompt guidance, or deleting the safety requirement.
analysis.calibration_use: Use graph evidence to find universal choke points, while requiring explicit handling of legitimate exceptions.

distractor_rationales.B: One patch leaves the stated systemic inconsistency.
distractor_rationales.C: Prompt text cannot enforce runtime authorization.
distractor_rationales.D: Removing permissions violates the safety objective.

scenario: Only ImageGenerateTool needs to persist generated asset metadata because it alone produces durable assets. Other tools return ephemeral strings and the shared base deliberately knows nothing about asset semantics.
user_request: Choose the implementation boundary.

choices.A: Put asset persistence in every tool invocation and create empty ledger rows for string tools.
choices.B: Teach the base class image-specific fields and dependencies.
choices.C: Implement persistence in the image-generation boundary using the shared asset service, leaving unrelated tools and the generic base unchanged.
choices.D: Skip persistence for images because centralization is impossible.

gold_rationale: Asset durability is specific to one producer type, while a reusable asset service can still own storage mechanics. Keeping orchestration at the image boundary preserves the generic tool contract.

analysis.hypothesis: The model resists centralizing domain-specific behavior into a universal base merely because a choke point exists.
analysis.decisive_information: Only image generation creates durable assets and the base intentionally has no asset contract.
analysis.variant_axis: A universal pre-execution permission invariant in v1 becomes producer-specific post-result persistence.
analysis.failure_signal: Empty artifacts for unrelated tools, base-class domain leakage, or abandoning required persistence.
analysis.calibration_use: Require both reachability and semantic universality before placing behavior at a shared choke point.

distractor_rationales.A: Unrelated string tools should not create asset records.
distractor_rationales.B: Image-specific dependencies pollute the generic base contract.
distractor_rationales.D: A specific boundary plus shared service satisfies persistence cleanly.

scenario: A new parser replaces an old parser, but two supported plugins still import the old public function. The goal is eventual removal without breaking the current release.
user_request: Choose the implementation strategy.

choices.A: Delete the old function immediately and let plugins fail.
choices.B: Keep a tested compatibility adapter with deprecation telemetry/documentation, migrate known consumers, and remove it only after the supported window/gate.
choices.C: Duplicate both full implementations indefinitely.
choices.D: Silently make the old function return different semantics.

gold_rationale: The old path remains a supported public dependency. A thin observable adapter enables migration and a verifiable removal gate without maintaining two divergent implementations or breaking the release.

analysis.hypothesis: The model handles obsolete public paths through bounded migration rather than immediate deletion or permanent duplication.
analysis.decisive_information: Two supported external plugins still import the old function and removal is an eventual goal.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant proves the old private path has no consumers and is unreachable.
analysis.failure_signal: Premature breakage, indefinite dual logic, or silent semantic incompatibility.
analysis.calibration_use: Use consumer evidence and support windows to choose adapter, migration, and deletion gates.

distractor_rationales.A: Immediate deletion breaks supported consumers.
distractor_rationales.C: Two implementations create indefinite drift.
distractor_rationales.D: Silent semantic change violates compatibility.

scenario: The old parser is private, static and runtime searches find no callers, tests or reflective registrations. The new parser covers all behavior, and keeping both causes duplicate maintenance.
user_request: Choose the implementation strategy.

choices.A: Keep the unreachable parser forever in case evidence is wrong.
choices.B: Add a public deprecation protocol for a private unused symbol.
choices.C: Route random requests to the old parser for comparison without need.
choices.D: Remove the proven-unreachable old path, clean related dead tests/docs if any, and run regression checks on the surviving parser.

gold_rationale: Authoritative searches establish no consumer or registration boundary, and the replacement fully covers behavior. Removing dead private code reduces maintenance without a compatibility layer that serves nobody.

analysis.hypothesis: The model completes simplification when evidence proves an obsolete private path has no compatibility obligation.
analysis.decisive_information: No callers, tests, reflection, or registrations reach the private parser and replacement coverage exists.
analysis.variant_axis: A publicly consumed old function in v1 becomes a verified unreachable private path.
analysis.failure_signal: Permanent dead code, invented public process, or unnecessary random routing.
analysis.calibration_use: Gate deletion on multi-channel reachability evidence, then prefer removal over defensive indefinite duplication.

distractor_rationales.A: Evidence supports safe removal and indefinite retention has cost.
distractor_rationales.B: No public consumer exists to deprecate.
distractor_rationales.C: Random routing reintroduces an obsolete implementation without purpose.

scenario: A bug report supplies input '1e-' that crashes parse_number(). No existing test exercises malformed exponents, and the pre-fix code reproduces the crash reliably.
user_request: Choose the testing sequence.

choices.A: Add a focused regression that fails on the pre-fix code with the reported input, implement the fix, then run related parser and broader checks.
choices.B: Fix first and write a test that can only pass afterward without proving reproduction.
choices.C: Run only unrelated UI tests.
choices.D: Delete the malformed input from documentation.

gold_rationale: A pre-fix failing regression establishes that the test detects the reported mechanism rather than merely exercising the changed code. Related and broad checks then cover collateral parser behavior.

analysis.hypothesis: The model creates discriminating evidence for a reproducible defect before relying on a post-fix passing test.
analysis.decisive_information: The exact crashing input is known, deterministic, and currently uncovered.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant has an existing regression already proven to fail before the implementation change.
analysis.failure_signal: Non-discriminating post-hoc tests, irrelevant suites, or removing the report rather than testing behavior.
analysis.calibration_use: Prompt for pre-fix reproduction when feasible and record whether a regression distinguishes old from new behavior.

distractor_rationales.B: A post-only pass may not demonstrate that the test detects the bug.
distractor_rationales.C: UI tests do not cover number parsing.
distractor_rationales.D: Documentation removal does not fix the crash.

scenario: An existing test test_malformed_exponent is already recorded failing on the pre-fix commit with input '1e-' and passes only after the current one-line parser fix. Its assertion matches the requested error result exactly.
user_request: Choose the testing sequence.

choices.A: Add five duplicate tests with the identical input before reading the existing one.
choices.B: Delete the existing discriminating test and recreate it under another name.
choices.C: Use the proven existing regression as focused feedback, add new cases only for uncovered boundaries, then run related and broader checks.
choices.D: Refuse the fix because the test now passes.

gold_rationale: The existing test already provides the required before/after discrimination and exact assertion. Duplicating it adds no coverage; effort should target adjacent uncovered cases and regression scope.

analysis.hypothesis: The model reuses proven regression evidence and avoids cargo-cult duplication when coverage already exists.
analysis.decisive_information: The test is demonstrated to fail before, pass after, and assert the exact requested behavior.
analysis.variant_axis: No relevant test in v1 becomes a fully discriminating existing regression.
analysis.failure_signal: Duplicate coverage, deleting valid evidence, or interpreting a post-fix pass as a reason to reject the fix.
analysis.calibration_use: Retrieve and evaluate existing tests before generating new ones, focusing additions on uncovered failure partitions.

distractor_rationales.A: Identical duplicates add no behavioral coverage.
distractor_rationales.B: Renaming the same test destroys history without value.
distractor_rationales.D: Passing after the fix is the intended regression outcome.

scenario: A pure normalize_name(value) function has no I/O, global state, or framework wiring. The change concerns trimming one Unicode whitespace category and preserving all other characters.
user_request: Choose the primary regression level.

choices.A: Launch the entire TUI and inspect pixels manually for every string.
choices.B: Add focused unit cases for the Unicode boundary and nearby non-whitespace characters, then run consumers' related tests.
choices.C: Provision a production database.
choices.D: Mock the function so its body never executes.

gold_rationale: The behavior is a deterministic pure transformation, so focused input/output unit cases directly exercise the mechanism. Related consumer tests provide proportionate integration confidence afterward.

analysis.hypothesis: The model selects unit tests for isolated deterministic logic and adds integration only where consumers may be affected.
analysis.decisive_information: The function is pure and the defect is one exact character-class boundary.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant keeps helper logic correct but breaks dependency injection wiring at runtime.
analysis.failure_signal: Expensive unrelated end-to-end setup, irrelevant database use, or mocking away the code under test.
analysis.calibration_use: Map failure location and dependencies to the lowest test level that directly observes the behavior.

distractor_rationales.A: A full visual TUI path is indirect for pure normalization.
distractor_rationales.C: No database participates in the function.
distractor_rationales.D: Mocking the target prevents testing its behavior.

scenario: The normalization helper's unit tests pass, but the production bug occurs because the CLI container wires LegacyNormalizer instead of the new Normalizer. The registration path is executed only when the application starts.
user_request: Choose the primary regression level.

choices.A: Add more unit cases to the already-correct helper only.
choices.B: Mock the container to return whichever class the test expects.
choices.C: Test an unrelated parser module.
choices.D: Add an integration test that builds the real CLI container and asserts the resolved normalizer/observable behavior, retaining unit coverage for helper logic.

gold_rationale: The defect is in application wiring, not normalization semantics. A real-container integration test exercises the registration boundary that unit tests and mocked resolution bypass.

analysis.hypothesis: The model raises test level when the failure mechanism lies in runtime composition rather than isolated logic.
analysis.decisive_information: The correct helper exists and passes units, but startup resolves the wrong implementation.
analysis.variant_axis: A pure helper defect in v1 becomes a container registration defect.
analysis.failure_signal: More irrelevant unit cases, mocking away the wrong wiring, or testing another subsystem.
analysis.calibration_use: Require tests to cross the boundary where the incorrect implementation is selected.

distractor_rationales.A: Helper units cannot observe container selection.
distractor_rationales.B: Mocking resolution hides the production wiring defect.
distractor_rationales.C: An unrelated parser provides no evidence.

scenario: An async queue occasionally emits the same job twice when cancellation races with acknowledgement. A single sequential run usually passes; the code uses two interleaving tasks and a controllable synchronization hook exists.
user_request: Choose the regression design.

choices.A: Run one sequential happy-path example.
choices.B: Add arbitrary sleep(5) calls and hope timing reproduces the race.
choices.C: Use the synchronization hook to deterministically force the cancel/ack interleaving, assert exactly-once behavior, and repeat a bounded stress variant.
choices.D: Mock the queue so no tasks run.

gold_rationale: The failure depends on a specific interleaving, and the hook makes that schedule controllable. A deterministic race regression plus bounded stress provides stronger evidence than sleeps or sequential execution.

analysis.hypothesis: The model tests concurrency mechanisms by controlling interleavings rather than relying on incidental timing.
analysis.decisive_information: The cancel/ack schedule causes the defect and an explicit synchronization hook can force it.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is a deterministic single-threaded calculation with no shared state.
analysis.failure_signal: Sequential false confidence, sleep-based flakiness, or mocking away concurrency.
analysis.calibration_use: Prefer deterministic barriers/hooks for race regressions and supplement them with bounded stress where useful.

distractor_rationales.A: Sequential execution cannot exercise the race.
distractor_rationales.B: Fixed sleeps are slow and timing-dependent.
distractor_rationales.D: A mocked queue removes the interleaving under test.

scenario: A single-threaded calculate_fee(amount, rate) function has no async calls, mutable globals, clocks, or shared resources. The bug is an incorrect decimal rounding boundary at exactly 0.005.
user_request: Choose the regression design.

choices.A: Add deterministic boundary-value unit cases around 0.005 and the specified rounding mode.
choices.B: Run 100 concurrent workers to test a nonexistent race.
choices.C: Insert random sleeps around arithmetic.
choices.D: Require a distributed load environment before testing.

gold_rationale: The defect is pure deterministic arithmetic at a known boundary. Direct unit cases around that partition precisely cover it; concurrency and load add no relevant mechanism.

analysis.hypothesis: The model does not apply concurrency testing universally after seeing a paired race scenario.
analysis.decisive_information: The function is single-threaded and pure, with a specific numeric boundary defect.
analysis.variant_axis: A two-task cancellation race in v1 becomes isolated deterministic arithmetic.
analysis.failure_signal: Invented concurrency, timing noise, or disproportionate distributed setup.
analysis.calibration_use: Classify state-sharing and scheduling dependencies before selecting race, stress, or ordinary boundary tests.

distractor_rationales.B: Workers do not improve coverage of pure rounding semantics.
distractor_rationales.C: Sleeps cannot affect deterministic arithmetic correctly.
distractor_rationales.D: Distributed load is unrelated to the failure.

scenario: A parser must round-trip arbitrary valid key/value maps: decode(encode(x)) == x. The input space includes escaped delimiters, Unicode, empty strings, and nested lengths; hand-written examples cover only five combinations.
user_request: Choose the additional test strategy.

choices.A: Add one more ordinary ASCII example and declare exhaustive coverage.
choices.B: Snapshot the source code text.
choices.C: Generate only invalid inputs and never test valid round trips.
choices.D: Add property-based generation for valid structured maps with shrinking, retain targeted regressions for known edge cases, and assert the round-trip invariant.

gold_rationale: The requirement is an invariant over a combinatorial structured input space, which property-based generation and shrinking can explore far beyond a few examples while preserving explicit regressions.

analysis.hypothesis: The model chooses property-based tests when the contract is a broad invariant over combinatorial inputs.
analysis.decisive_information: Round-trip equality applies to arbitrary valid maps with many interacting dimensions.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is a fixed legal mapping with exactly four enumerated inputs.
analysis.failure_signal: Tiny example extrapolation, source snapshots, or testing only the opposite validity domain.
analysis.calibration_use: Detect algebraic/invariant-style contracts and recommend generators plus shrinking alongside known regressions.

distractor_rationales.A: One ASCII case barely expands the combinatorial space.
distractor_rationales.B: Source text does not test parser semantics.
distractor_rationales.C: Invalid inputs cannot establish valid round-trip behavior.

scenario: A function maps the four exact enum members RED, GREEN, BLUE, and UNKNOWN to four legally mandated fixed labels. No other input is accepted and schema validation rejects it before the function.
user_request: Choose the test strategy.

choices.A: Generate arbitrary nested maps despite the closed four-value domain.
choices.B: Write an explicit parameterized table covering all four enum-to-label mappings plus schema rejection at its own boundary.
choices.C: Test only RED and assume symmetry.
choices.D: Fuzz operating-system processes.

gold_rationale: The accepted domain is finite, tiny, and fully enumerable. A four-row parameterized test is exhaustive and clearer than unconstrained generation, while validation remains tested at its actual boundary.

analysis.hypothesis: The model prefers explicit exhaustive enumeration when the valid domain is small and closed.
analysis.decisive_information: Exactly four schema-validated enum inputs can reach the function.
analysis.variant_axis: A combinatorial open structured space in v1 becomes a closed enumerable domain.
analysis.failure_signal: Misapplied property generation, incomplete one-case inference, or unrelated process fuzzing.
analysis.calibration_use: Choose property generation versus parameterization based on domain cardinality and invariant structure.

distractor_rationales.A: Arbitrary maps are outside the accepted enum domain.
distractor_rationales.C: One member does not exhaust four legally distinct labels.
distractor_rationales.D: OS fuzzing has no relation to enum mapping.

scenario: A TUI widget regression concerns exact borders, colors, spacing, and wrapping at three terminal widths. A deterministic renderer can produce normalized screen snapshots with volatile timestamps masked.
user_request: Choose the regression evidence.

choices.A: Inspect only the widget constructor's return type.
choices.B: Assert the rendered string contains one word.
choices.C: Use reviewed normalized snapshots at the three widths plus targeted semantic assertions for critical controls.
choices.D: Snapshot random memory addresses and timestamps.

gold_rationale: The defect is a multi-dimensional visual layout contract that deterministic width-specific snapshots capture well. Stable normalization prevents noise, and semantic assertions protect important interaction meaning.

analysis.hypothesis: The model uses snapshots when broad structured presentation is itself the contract and output can be stabilized.
analysis.decisive_information: Borders, colors, spacing, and wrapping across known widths are all required and deterministically renderable.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant changes the requirement to semantic JSON equivalence where field order is irrelevant.
analysis.failure_signal: Shallow type/token checks or snapshots polluted by volatile values.
analysis.calibration_use: Recommend snapshots for stable high-dimensional presentation, paired with semantic assertions for critical behavior.

distractor_rationales.A: Constructor type does not expose rendered layout.
distractor_rationales.B: One word cannot cover borders, colors, spacing, or wrapping.
distractor_rationales.D: Volatile data creates meaningless snapshot churn.

scenario: An API returns JSON where object key order and whitespace are explicitly irrelevant. The requirement is that required fields, numeric values, and error semantics remain correct across serializers.
user_request: Choose the regression evidence.

choices.A: Parse responses and assert the semantic structure/values and error contract, avoiding raw-text snapshots that fail on harmless ordering.
choices.B: Snapshot exact whitespace and dictionary order from one runtime.
choices.C: Assert only that the response is nonempty.
choices.D: Compare terminal colors.

gold_rationale: The contract explicitly excludes serialization formatting. Structural assertions cover required semantics while raw snapshots would create false failures from permitted key order or whitespace changes.

analysis.hypothesis: The model avoids snapshot testing when representation details are outside the contract and would make tests brittle.
analysis.decisive_information: Key order and whitespace are irrelevant, while parsed fields and error behavior are normative.
analysis.variant_axis: A stable visual representation contract in v1 becomes representation-independent structured semantics.
analysis.failure_signal: Brittle raw snapshots, existence-only checks, or testing unrelated visual properties.
analysis.calibration_use: Ask whether representation is normative before choosing exact snapshots versus semantic comparisons.

distractor_rationales.B: It asserts details the API explicitly permits to vary.
distractor_rationales.C: Nonempty output does not validate fields or errors.
distractor_rationales.D: Terminal colors are unrelated to JSON semantics.

scenario: A billing service calculates retry decisions from provider error classes. Unit tests need deterministic coverage of every documented provider response without network access; a small provider protocol is already defined.
user_request: Choose the test double strategy.

choices.A: Patch internal private methods throughout the billing service.
choices.B: Use a fake/stub implementing the provider protocol to return each documented response, and separately keep a contract/integration check against the real adapter.
choices.C: Call production billing for every unit test.
choices.D: Mock the billing decision function itself.

gold_rationale: The provider protocol is the natural seam for deterministic unit scenarios, while a separate adapter contract test guards against fake drift. Mocking the subject or private internals would hide behavior.

analysis.hypothesis: The model places doubles at an explicit external boundary and preserves a test that validates the real adapter contract.
analysis.decisive_information: A provider protocol exists and network responses must be simulated deterministically for decision logic.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant concerns serialization behavior unique to the real third-party sandbox and absent from the protocol fake.
analysis.failure_signal: Brittle internal patching, production side effects, or mocking away the logic under test.
analysis.calibration_use: Prefer interface-level fakes for unit control and pair them with contract evidence that the adapter matches reality.

distractor_rationales.A: Private-method patching couples tests to implementation details.
distractor_rationales.C: Production billing is unsafe and nondeterministic for unit tests.
distractor_rationales.D: Mocking the decision function prevents testing it.

scenario: A defect occurs because the real payment sandbox serializes duplicate headers differently from the local fake. The fake's protocol omits raw header multiplicity, and all unit tests pass.
user_request: Choose the primary regression evidence.

choices.A: Add another expectation to the same incapable fake.
choices.B: Mock the serializer result to the desired value.
choices.C: Test only the downstream error string.
choices.D: Add a sandbox/adapter integration regression exercising the real duplicate-header serialization, then update the protocol/fake only if the production contract should expose it.

gold_rationale: The failure exists specifically in behavior the fake cannot represent. A real adapter boundary test is required to reproduce it; afterward the abstraction can be corrected rather than teaching the fake an unsupported fiction.

analysis.hypothesis: The model abandons a test double when the defect lies in omitted real-boundary semantics.
analysis.decisive_information: Only the real sandbox exposes duplicate-header serialization and the fake lacks that dimension.
analysis.variant_axis: Decision logic representable by a provider protocol in v1 becomes adapter-specific behavior outside the fake.
analysis.failure_signal: More false fake confidence, mocking the expected result, or asserting only a downstream symptom.
analysis.calibration_use: Detect when test doubles cannot express the failure mechanism and route coverage to a controlled real boundary.

distractor_rationales.A: The fake cannot represent the relevant raw multiplicity.
distractor_rationales.B: Mocking the desired serialization assumes the answer.
distractor_rationales.C: A downstream string does not verify the adapter defect.

scenario: A live schema migration backfills NULL status values, supports old and new app versions during rollout, and later enforces NOT NULL. Most risk lies in upgrading populated legacy databases.
user_request: Choose the migration test matrix.

choices.A: Test only creating an empty database at the final schema.
choices.B: Inspect SQL formatting without executing it.
choices.C: Create representative pre-migration data, run each migration/rolling compatibility step, verify backfill and old/new reads/writes, then validate the final constraint and restart path.
choices.D: Mock the database so no DDL runs.

gold_rationale: The risky behavior is transition of real legacy state under mixed versions, not final empty initialization. Executing the sequence with representative data directly covers backfill, compatibility, constraint, and restart invariants.

analysis.hypothesis: The model tests state transitions from realistic prior versions rather than only the final schema shape.
analysis.decisive_information: Populated NULL rows and old/new version overlap are the primary migration risks.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is a brand-new empty schema with no upgrade path or old version.
analysis.failure_signal: Final-state-only false confidence, non-executing format checks, or mocking away DDL.
analysis.calibration_use: Derive migration fixtures from supported starting states and execute the complete upgrade compatibility sequence.

distractor_rationales.A: Empty final creation misses legacy backfill and rolling compatibility.
distractor_rationales.B: Formatted SQL can still fail or transform data incorrectly.
distractor_rationales.D: A mocked database cannot validate actual DDL/data transitions.

scenario: The product has never shipped and initializes an empty database directly from one final schema. There are no prior versions, legacy rows, downgrade promises, or rolling instances.
user_request: Choose the schema test matrix.

choices.A: Test fresh initialization, required defaults/constraints, and representative first writes; do not invent unsupported upgrade histories.
choices.B: Manufacture ten fictional old versions and require migrations from each.
choices.C: Skip schema tests because the database is new.
choices.D: Test only a downgrade contract that does not exist.

gold_rationale: Only fresh initialization and first-use invariants are supported behaviors. Testing them directly is complete for the stated lifecycle; fictional upgrade matrices add maintenance without product evidence.

analysis.hypothesis: The model avoids fabricating migration test obligations when no prior supported state exists.
analysis.decisive_information: There are no shipped versions, data, rolling overlap, or downgrade contract.
analysis.variant_axis: A populated live upgrade in v1 becomes a first-release empty initialization.
analysis.failure_signal: Invented history, total absence of schema checks, or testing an unsupported downgrade.
analysis.calibration_use: Build test matrices from actual supported lifecycle states rather than generic migration ceremony.

distractor_rationales.B: Fictional versions are not supported inputs.
distractor_rationales.C: Fresh schema constraints and writes still require verification.
distractor_rationales.D: No downgrade behavior was promised.

scenario: An outbox worker must recover if the external provider accepts a request but the local process crashes before recording success. The provider supports idempotency and the worker has injectable crash points.
user_request: Choose the resilience test.

choices.A: Test only the all-success path.
choices.B: Mock away persistence and provider calls together.
choices.C: Assert the source contains the word retry.
choices.D: Inject a crash at the accepted-before-record boundary, restart from durable state, and assert idempotent reconciliation without duplicate external effects.

gold_rationale: The invariant is specifically about ambiguous outcome across a crash boundary. Controlled failure and restart exercise durable recovery and idempotency, which happy-path or textual tests cannot establish.

analysis.hypothesis: The model tests recovery guarantees by inducing failure at the exact persistence/external-effect boundary.
analysis.decisive_information: A crash after provider acceptance but before local recording is the named risk and is injectable.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is a pure function with no state, side effects, or recovery behavior.
analysis.failure_signal: Happy-path-only evidence, mocking away both state systems, or source-token assertions.
analysis.calibration_use: Map resilience claims to explicit failure points and require restart/reconciliation observations at those boundaries.

distractor_rationales.A: Success execution does not cover crash recovery.
distractor_rationales.B: Removing persistence and provider effects removes the invariant.
distractor_rationales.C: A keyword does not prove recovery behavior.

scenario: A pure format_label(name) function has no I/O, durable state, retries, clocks, processes, or external effects. The requirement is exact escaping of '&' and '<'.
user_request: Choose the regression test.

choices.A: Kill the test runner during every assertion.
choices.B: Use direct deterministic input/output cases for escaping and nearby unaffected characters.
choices.C: Provision an external provider and simulate network partition.
choices.D: Restart a database that the function never uses.

gold_rationale: The contract is pure deterministic escaping with no recovery boundary. Direct examples precisely test the behavior; crash, network, and database injection add unrelated failure modes.

analysis.hypothesis: The model does not carry resilience-testing machinery into code that has no stateful failure boundary.
analysis.decisive_information: The function is pure and the exact escaping inputs and outputs are specified.
analysis.variant_axis: A distributed crash-recovery invariant in v1 becomes isolated string transformation.
analysis.failure_signal: Disproportionate fault injection or infrastructure unrelated to the target function.
analysis.calibration_use: Require an actual recoverable state/effect boundary before recommending failure-injection tests.

distractor_rationales.A: Runner termination does not test escaping semantics.
distractor_rationales.C: No network provider participates.
distractor_rationales.D: No database participates.

scenario: A change modifies a helper used only by one parser module. Blast-radius inspection finds no other importers, focused regression and parser-file tests pass, and the project requires a full suite before handoff.
user_request: Choose the verification sequence.

choices.A: Iterate with the focused regression and related parser tests, then run the required full suite once the fix stabilizes.
choices.B: Run only the full suite repeatedly and never isolate failures.
choices.C: Skip the required suite because focused tests passed.
choices.D: Run no tests and rely on blast-radius output.

gold_rationale: Focused tests optimize diagnostic feedback during iteration, while the repository's completion gate still requires the full suite. The sequence preserves both efficiency and broad handoff evidence.

analysis.hypothesis: The model separates iterative test selection from mandatory final verification rather than choosing one forever.
analysis.decisive_information: The defect is localized, focused tests exist, and project policy explicitly requires a final full suite.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant changes a shared fixture whose risk requires broad tests immediately.
analysis.failure_signal: Only-broad slow diagnosis, skipping the final gate, or treating static impact analysis as runtime proof.
analysis.calibration_use: Plan test ladders with distinct iteration and completion phases, honoring explicit repository gates.

distractor_rationales.B: Repeated full suites slow local diagnosis unnecessarily.
distractor_rationales.C: Focused success does not waive the explicit final gate.
distractor_rationales.D: Impact analysis does not execute behavior.

scenario: A change modifies the autouse fixture that resets global database and thread-local state for nearly every test. The suspected defect appears only through cross-module order interactions, not in the fixture's own unit test.
user_request: Choose the verification sequence.

choices.A: Run only the fixture unit test until it passes.
choices.B: Run one parser test and extrapolate globally.
choices.C: Run broad suite/order-sensitive coverage early, use targeted reproductions for observed leaks, and repeat the full gate after the fix.
choices.D: Skip runtime tests because the fixture code is short.

gold_rationale: The changed fixture is a shared state boundary and the failure mechanism requires interactions across tests. Broad execution is diagnostic here, supplemented by focused reproductions once failing orders are known.

analysis.hypothesis: The model moves broad tests earlier when the defect cannot manifest within a localized test scope.
analysis.decisive_information: Nearly all tests consume the fixture and the suspected failure is cross-module/order-dependent.
analysis.variant_axis: A localized helper with a mandatory final suite in v1 becomes a cross-cutting fixture requiring broad diagnostic execution.
analysis.failure_signal: Local-only false confidence, one-sample extrapolation, or code-length-based test skipping.
analysis.calibration_use: Use blast radius and failure mechanism to decide whether broad tests are a final gate or an early diagnostic tool.

distractor_rationales.A: The unit test cannot expose consumer order interactions.
distractor_rationales.B: One consumer is not representative of a global fixture.
distractor_rationales.D: Short code can still corrupt shared state broadly.

scenario: A new regression fails 3 of 20 runs on unchanged code and passes after immediate reruns. Logs show it waits for a background event without synchronization; the production behavior under test is deterministic.
user_request: Choose how to handle the test.

choices.A: Accept it because most runs pass.
choices.B: Treat the nondeterminism as a test defect: replace timing guesses with synchronization, demonstrate repeated stability, and keep the behavioral assertion.
choices.C: Add automatic retries until green and hide first failures.
choices.D: Delete the assertion so the test cannot fail.

gold_rationale: The underlying contract is deterministic, while missing synchronization makes the test schedule-dependent. Repairing the test mechanism preserves coverage and avoids masking real regressions with retries.

analysis.hypothesis: The model diagnoses and removes accidental test nondeterminism rather than normalizing retries or weakened assertions.
analysis.decisive_information: Unchanged deterministic behavior yields intermittent results because the test lacks event synchronization.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant is a deliberately randomized property test with reproducible seeds and statistical acceptance criteria.
analysis.failure_signal: Majority-pass acceptance, hidden retry success, or deleting meaningful coverage.
analysis.calibration_use: Classify accidental versus intentional randomness and require reproducibility before accepting stochastic tests.

distractor_rationales.A: Intermittent false results undermine suite trust.
distractor_rationales.C: Retries conceal the race without fixing test validity.
distractor_rationales.D: Removing the assertion removes regression coverage.

scenario: A randomized property test samples valid parser structures using a recorded seed, shrinks failures to deterministic cases, and its predefined campaign requires 10,000 samples with a zero-failure threshold. The same seed reproduces any failure exactly.
user_request: Choose how to handle the test.

choices.A: Remove all randomness because every varied input is flaky.
choices.B: Ignore failures if a different seed passes.
choices.C: Replace 10,000 samples with one hand-picked example.
choices.D: Keep the intentional seeded campaign, record failing seeds/shrunk cases, and treat any threshold violation as reproducible evidence rather than accidental flakiness.

gold_rationale: Random input diversity is intentional and controlled: seeds reproduce executions, shrinking localizes failures, and acceptance was defined in advance. This is stochastic coverage, not uncontrolled flakiness.

analysis.hypothesis: The model distinguishes controlled randomized testing from timing-dependent nondeterminism.
analysis.decisive_information: Every run is seed-recorded and reproducible, with shrinking and a predefined zero-failure campaign.
analysis.variant_axis: An unsynchronized accidental race in v1 becomes intentional reproducible input randomization.
analysis.failure_signal: Blanket randomness removal, seed shopping, or collapsing broad property coverage to one example.
analysis.calibration_use: Judge stochastic tests by reproducibility, predefined criteria, and failure minimization rather than variation alone.

distractor_rationales.A: Controlled random generation provides valuable domain coverage.
distractor_rationales.B: A passing different seed does not erase a reproducible failure.
distractor_rationales.C: One example cannot replace the intended property campaign.

scenario: A patch changes pagination from items[start:start + limit] to items[start:start + limit - 1]. The API contract says limit is the maximum number of returned items, and an existing test expects 10 items for limit=10.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Flag an off-by-one correctness regression: positive limits now return one fewer item; cite the changed slice and add/retain boundary tests.
choices.B: Approve because subtracting one is usually safer.
choices.C: Request renaming items for style only.
choices.D: Claim SQL injection despite no SQL.

gold_rationale: Python slice ends are exclusive, so subtracting one violates the documented maximum-count behavior and contradicts an existing boundary test. The finding is concrete and reproducible.

analysis.hypothesis: The model identifies a concrete semantic regression from language behavior and contract evidence.
analysis.decisive_information: Slice end is exclusive, the contract defines count semantics, and limit=10 must yield 10 items.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant changes an inclusive database range into the correct count calculation.
analysis.failure_signal: Approving a proven regression, style distraction, or inventing an unrelated vulnerability.
analysis.calibration_use: Require review findings to connect changed lines, executable semantics, and a violated contract/test.

distractor_rationales.B: The change reduces valid results contrary to contract.
distractor_rationales.C: Naming preference does not address the correctness defect.
distractor_rationales.D: No database query or injection surface exists.

scenario: A database API uses an inclusive end index. The patch changes end = start + limit to end = start + limit - 1 so requesting limit=10 returns indices start through start+9. Tests cover limits 1 and 10.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Flag the minus one as automatically wrong because another language's slices are exclusive.
choices.B: Claim pagination must return limit+1 items.
choices.C: Do not flag an off-by-one: for this documented inclusive API, the new calculation correctly returns exactly limit items; review other risks normally.
choices.D: Demand replacement with a Python slice even though this is a database range API.

gold_rationale: Inclusive ranges contain end-start+1 elements, so subtracting one is required to return exactly limit items. The matching tests corroborate the corrected semantics.

analysis.hypothesis: The model evaluates boundary semantics in the actual API rather than pattern-matching on suspicious arithmetic.
analysis.decisive_information: The end index is inclusive and tests confirm exact counts at key boundaries.
analysis.variant_axis: An exclusive Python slice in v1 becomes an inclusive database range.
analysis.failure_signal: Language-semantics transfer, inventing limit+1 requirements, or prescribing an incompatible primitive.
analysis.calibration_use: Provide reviewers with API-specific range semantics and reward justified non-findings on superficially similar diffs.

distractor_rationales.A: Minus one is correct under inclusive-end semantics.
distractor_rationales.B: The contract requests exactly limit items, not limit+1.
distractor_rationales.D: The database API cannot be replaced by a local slice without changing behavior.

scenario: A patch builds SQL as f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{user_name}'". user_name comes directly from an HTTP query parameter and the database driver supports bound parameters.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Approve because f-strings escape SQL automatically.
choices.B: Flag SQL injection at the interpolation line and require a bound parameter, with a malicious-quote regression test.
choices.C: Request a shorter variable name only.
choices.D: Suggest base64-encoding input as SQL protection.

gold_rationale: Untrusted HTTP input is inserted into SQL syntax without escaping or binding. The available parameter API separates data from code and directly removes the injection mechanism.

analysis.hypothesis: The model flags a concrete exploitable data-to-code path and proposes the correct boundary defense.
analysis.decisive_information: HTTP-controlled text is interpolated into executable SQL and parameter binding exists.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant uses a driver-bound placeholder while logging only a fixed query identifier.
analysis.failure_signal: Assuming interpolation escapes, style-only review, or proposing encoding that does not separate SQL syntax.
analysis.calibration_use: Trace attacker-controlled values to interpreters and require findings to name the sink and safe API.

distractor_rationales.A: F-strings perform no SQL escaping.
distractor_rationales.C: Naming does not mitigate the injection path.
distractor_rationales.D: Base64 text can still be unsafe and changes semantics without binding.

scenario: A patch executes cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', (user_name,)). user_name comes from HTTP input. The logged message contains only query_id='find_user', not parameter values or reconstructed SQL.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Flag injection because any query involving user input is vulnerable.
choices.B: Require manual quote escaping in addition to the bound parameter.
choices.C: Claim sensitive names leak through the fixed query ID.
choices.D: Do not flag SQL injection here: the driver binds the untrusted value as data and the logging path does not reconstruct the query.

gold_rationale: The placeholder and separate parameter tuple preserve the code/data boundary, and logging does not reintroduce the value. No injection path is evidenced in the described change.

analysis.hypothesis: The model recognizes a correctly defended interpreter boundary and avoids generic security accusations.
analysis.decisive_information: The driver receives SQL and user data separately, and logs contain no reconstructed SQL or value.
analysis.variant_axis: Raw string interpolation in v1 becomes proper parameter binding with safe logging.
analysis.failure_signal: Input-presence heuristic, redundant manual escaping, or invented log leakage.
analysis.calibration_use: Include safe counterexamples so security calibration rewards precise data-flow analysis rather than keyword matching.

distractor_rationales.A: User input is safe when correctly bound as data.
distractor_rationales.B: Manual escaping is unnecessary and can conflict with driver binding.
distractor_rationales.C: A fixed query identifier contains no user name.

scenario: A patch moves if job_id not in processed and processed.add(job_id) into two separately locked blocks. Two worker threads can both pass the check before either add, causing duplicate processing.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Approve because every individual set access is locked.
choices.B: Request replacing the set with a list for readability.
choices.C: Flag a check-then-act race: the membership test and insertion must be one atomic critical section or use an atomic reservation primitive.
choices.D: Claim a deadlock without any lock cycle.

gold_rationale: Per-operation locking does not protect the compound uniqueness invariant. An interleaving lets both workers observe absence and proceed, so reservation must be atomic.

analysis.hypothesis: The model reviews invariants across operations rather than counting lock statements.
analysis.decisive_information: The check and add occur under separate lock acquisitions and duplicate processing is prohibited.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant performs both operations within one critical section and moves work outside the lock.
analysis.failure_signal: Lock-presence approval, irrelevant collection preference, or unsupported deadlock claims.
analysis.calibration_use: Prompt reviewers to identify compound state invariants and construct concrete interleavings for concurrency findings.

distractor_rationales.A: Separate locks allow another thread between check and add.
distractor_rationales.B: A list would not make the compound action atomic.
distractor_rationales.D: No cyclic acquisition evidence supports deadlock.

scenario: A patch checks and inserts job_id inside one lock acquisition, records whether this worker reserved it, releases the lock, and only the reserving worker performs slow processing. No shared state is read outside the lock.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Do not flag the prior check-then-act race; the reservation is atomic and slow work correctly occurs after releasing the lock.
choices.B: Demand holding the lock during all slow processing.
choices.C: Claim duplicate processing without presenting an interleaving.
choices.D: Remove the lock because the code looks simple.

gold_rationale: One critical section protects the membership-and-insert invariant, and a local reservation flag safely determines ownership afterward. Releasing before slow work reduces contention without reopening reservation.

analysis.hypothesis: The model recognizes correct lock granularity and avoids demanding over-serialization.
analysis.decisive_information: Check and insertion are atomic, ownership is captured locally, and shared state is not reread unsafely.
analysis.variant_axis: Separated critical sections in v1 become one atomic reservation section.
analysis.failure_signal: Holding locks unnecessarily, race claims without possible interleaving, or removing needed synchronization.
analysis.calibration_use: Train reviews to validate an invariant and ownership handoff, not prefer maximal lock duration.

distractor_rationales.B: Slow work need not hold the reservation lock and would increase contention.
distractor_rationales.C: No duplicate-producing interleaving exists under the stated critical section.
distractor_rationales.D: Simplicity does not eliminate concurrent access.

scenario: A patch opens a temporary file, writes to it, and returns early on validation failure before close() or cleanup. This path runs repeatedly in a long-lived worker and tests can trigger it.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Approve because the operating system eventually closes all files.
choices.B: Request a different filename style.
choices.C: Claim a memory leak without mentioning the file.
choices.D: Flag the early-return file-descriptor/temp-file leak and use a context manager/finally cleanup, with a failure-path test.

gold_rationale: The validation branch bypasses cleanup in a long-lived process, so repeated failures retain descriptors and artifacts. Structured cleanup directly covers every exit path.

analysis.hypothesis: The model traces ownership across exceptional/early exits and reports the concrete leaked resource.
analysis.decisive_information: The file opens before validation and the failure return bypasses both close and temp cleanup repeatedly.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant wraps ownership in a context manager and unlinks in finally.
analysis.failure_signal: Relying on process exit, style distraction, or vague misclassified leak claims.
analysis.calibration_use: Review every acquired resource against all exits and require findings to identify the unbalanced path.

distractor_rationales.A: Long-lived workers may exhaust descriptors before process exit.
distractor_rationales.B: Naming does not repair lifecycle ownership.
distractor_rationales.C: The concrete issue is file/temp resource cleanup, not unspecified heap growth.

scenario: A patch creates the temporary file inside a context manager and unlinks its path in a finally block. Validation may return early, but both context exit and finally execute; a test asserts no descriptor or file remains.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Flag a leak solely because an early return exists.
choices.B: Do not flag the described resource leak; structured cleanup covers early return and the failure-path test verifies it.
choices.C: Demand process termination after each file.
choices.D: Remove the finally block so the code is shorter.

gold_rationale: Python executes context-manager exit and finally on return, balancing both descriptor and filesystem artifact ownership. The targeted test corroborates the lifecycle behavior.

analysis.hypothesis: The model reasons through cleanup semantics rather than flagging any early return after acquisition.
analysis.decisive_information: Both cleanup mechanisms execute on return and a failure-path test observes no residue.
analysis.variant_axis: Unbalanced manual cleanup in v1 becomes structured lifecycle management.
analysis.failure_signal: Keyword-based leak accusation, extreme process workaround, or deleting required cleanup.
analysis.calibration_use: Include language control-flow semantics and failure-path tests as evidence that can dismiss suspected leaks.

distractor_rationales.A: Early return still triggers context exit and finally.
distractor_rationales.C: Per-file process termination is unnecessary.
distractor_rationales.D: Removing cleanup would reintroduce the leak.

scenario: A patch removes the legacy model_id JSON field from a public response immediately. The release notes promise it through version 2, telemetry shows active v1 clients, and no alias or version boundary is added.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Flag a backward-compatibility regression: active promised clients lose a required field; preserve/version/deprecate it with contract tests.
choices.B: Approve because the new field name is cleaner.
choices.C: Request alphabetic JSON key order only.
choices.D: Claim internal callers will automatically adapt over the network.

gold_rationale: The changed wire schema violates an explicit support promise and observed active consumers. A migration boundary and contract coverage are required before removal.

analysis.hypothesis: The model treats documented public behavior and consumer evidence as concrete regression constraints.
analysis.decisive_information: Version-2 support is promised, v1 clients are active, and the patch removes the field without transition.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant removes a private unused temporary key with all internal consumers updated.
analysis.failure_signal: Aesthetic approval, irrelevant ordering request, or assuming remote consumers update atomically.
analysis.calibration_use: Surface support windows and consumer telemetry during review of public schema changes.

distractor_rationales.B: Cleaner naming does not excuse contract breakage.
distractor_rationales.C: Key order is unrelated to the missing field.
distractor_rationales.D: External clients do not automatically change with server code.

scenario: A patch removes a private dictionary key _tmp_model_id used only within one function. All references in that function change atomically, searches find no reflection or serialization, and output contract tests are byte-identical.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Demand public API versioning for every private dictionary key.
choices.B: Claim external clients depend on the leading-underscore key without evidence.
choices.C: Do not flag backward compatibility: evidence shows the key is private, non-serialized, atomically migrated, and outputs are unchanged.
choices.D: Keep dead keys forever.

gold_rationale: No public or reflective boundary exposes the temporary key, all consumers change together, and byte-identical contract tests confirm external behavior. Public migration machinery is unwarranted.

analysis.hypothesis: The model distinguishes public contracts from private implementation details using consumer and output evidence.
analysis.decisive_information: The key never serializes, has no hidden consumers, and all outputs remain identical.
analysis.variant_axis: An actively consumed promised public field in v1 becomes private atomic state.
analysis.failure_signal: Universal versioning demands, invented consumers, or permanent dead-state retention.
analysis.calibration_use: Require evidence of an external compatibility boundary before elevating a private refactor to a release blocker.

distractor_rationales.A: Private local state does not require public version negotiation.
distractor_rationales.B: No serialization or reflection evidence supports external use.
distractor_rationales.D: Dead internal keys add confusion without compatibility value.

scenario: A patch changes except SpecificProviderError: mark_failed() into except Exception: return None. The caller interprets None as 'no work' and acknowledges the queue message, so programming errors and provider failures are silently dropped.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Approve because broad catches make services resilient.
choices.B: Flag error swallowing/data loss: catch the expected provider error narrowly, preserve failure state/retry semantics, and let unexpected exceptions surface.
choices.C: Request changing None to an empty string only.
choices.D: Suggest deleting logs so failures are quieter.

gold_rationale: The broad catch converts every unexpected defect into a successful no-work acknowledgement, losing jobs and diagnostic evidence. Narrow expected handling preserves the queue and error contracts.

analysis.hypothesis: The model traces exception translation into downstream state rather than praising generic resilience.
analysis.decisive_information: None triggers acknowledgement, and Exception includes unexpected programming failures that should not be silently consumed.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant catches one documented optional-metadata error and returns a contract-defined fallback.
analysis.failure_signal: Broad-catch approval, cosmetic sentinel changes, or further suppression of evidence.
analysis.calibration_use: Review exception handlers by enumerating caught classes and the semantic effect of their returned/committed state.

distractor_rationales.A: Silent acknowledgement loses work rather than improving resilience.
distractor_rationales.C: A different sentinel does not restore error semantics.
distractor_rationales.D: Removing logs worsens diagnosability and loss.

scenario: A patch catches MissingOptionalMetadata only, logs at debug, and returns the documented empty metadata object. All other exceptions propagate; callers explicitly treat empty metadata as a valid optional case and do not acknowledge failed work.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Flag all exception catching as data loss.
choices.B: Demand crashing on optional missing metadata despite the documented fallback.
choices.C: Claim the handler catches programming errors, although it names one domain exception.
choices.D: Do not flag error swallowing: the catch is narrow, fallback is contract-defined, and unexpected failures still propagate.

gold_rationale: The handler translates one expected domain condition into its documented value without committing or hiding unrelated failures. That is controlled error semantics, not broad suppression.

analysis.hypothesis: The model recognizes legitimate narrow exception translation and avoids categorical catch-block findings.
analysis.decisive_information: Only MissingOptionalMetadata is caught, the fallback is specified, and all unexpected errors propagate.
analysis.variant_axis: Broad Exception with loss semantics in v1 becomes one expected domain mapping.
analysis.failure_signal: Universal anti-catch rules, contradicting the contract, or misrepresenting the caught class set.
analysis.calibration_use: Include safe error-translation counterexamples so review guidance remains conditional and evidence-driven.

distractor_rationales.A: Narrow expected translation is not data loss.
distractor_rationales.B: The contract explicitly permits an empty optional value.
distractor_rationales.C: Programming exceptions are not subclasses of the named domain case by assumption.

scenario: Inside a loop over every project, a patch calls database.load_members(project.id). Production can contain 50,000 projects, tracing shows one query per iteration, and the same data can be fetched in one batched query.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Approve because each individual query is fast.
choices.B: Request renaming the loop variable only.
choices.C: Flag an N+1 performance regression with production scale evidence; batch/prefetch members and add a query-count/scale regression.
choices.D: Suggest sleeping between queries.

gold_rationale: The new query count grows linearly to roughly 50,001 calls on realistic input, while a supported batch path exists. This is a concrete scale regression, not speculative micro-optimization.

analysis.hypothesis: The model prioritizes performance findings with demonstrated asymptotic or production-scale impact.
analysis.decisive_information: The loop reaches 50,000 items, tracing confirms per-item queries, and batching is available.
analysis.variant_axis: The paired variant bounds the collection to two items loaded once at startup.
analysis.failure_signal: Per-call latency myopia, style distraction, or adding delay to an already excessive query pattern.
analysis.calibration_use: Require scale bounds, observed operation counts, and a viable remedy for performance review findings.

distractor_rationales.A: Many fast queries still create major aggregate latency/load.
distractor_rationales.B: Naming does not change query complexity.
distractor_rationales.D: Sleeping increases latency and retains N+1 behavior.

scenario: A startup path loops over exactly two built-in roles, guaranteed by a closed enum, and performs one cached dictionary lookup per role. It runs once per process and profiling shows less than 5 microseconds total.
user_request: Choose the review finding.

choices.A: Do not raise a performance blocker: the loop is tightly bounded, uses in-memory cached lookups, and measured cost is negligible.
choices.B: Flag N+1 database queries even though no database is called.
choices.C: Demand a distributed batch service for two dictionary accesses.
choices.D: Claim quadratic behavior without nested growth.

gold_rationale: The operation count is fixed at two, purely in memory, startup-only, and directly measured as negligible. A performance finding would lack impact and mechanism.

analysis.hypothesis: The model avoids labeling every loop as a scalability defect when authoritative bounds and measurements refute impact.
analysis.decisive_information: Closed cardinality is two, no I/O occurs, and profiling shows negligible one-time cost.
analysis.variant_axis: An unbounded 50,000-item per-query loop in v1 becomes two cached lookups.
analysis.failure_signal: Loop keyword heuristics, invented I/O, disproportionate architecture, or unsupported complexity claims.
analysis.calibration_use: Reward reviewers for dismissing performance suspicions when bounds and profiling make impact immaterial.

distractor_rationales.B: No database operation exists in the loop.
distractor_rationales.C: A service would dwarf the measured local work.
distractor_rationales.D: One fixed loop is not quadratic.

scenario: A patch changes permission behavior so denied destructive tools now return a typed result instead of raising. Existing tests cover only allowed calls; no test verifies denial, side-effect absence, or the new result contract.
user_request: Choose the review finding.
